summary: The Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund (NB-FOETF), set up by Nigerian Breweries in 1994 with N100 million, funds classrooms and libraries, the Maltina Teacher of the Year competition, and scholarships for deserving students, including at tertiary level. As of October 2026 there is no open, public application call for a university scholarship on Nigerian Breweries' official site; recent awards (e.g. a July 2026 secondary-school scholarship) were made by recognition and through partners such as Slum2School Africa. Use this guide to stay ready, verify any call, and pursue similar awards.
lookfor: Official statements describe recipients as 'deserving' students with exceptional potential, often from underserved backgrounds
Recent recipients were identified through Trust Fund events and partner organisations, not an open form
If a public call appears, expect the usual Nigerian corporate criteria: strong CGPA, enrolment proof and genuine documents - check the call itself
No confirmed CGPA cut-off, level or deadline for a university award was published as of October 2026
cycle: No public university-scholarship application window was found for 2025-2027. The Trust Fund's visible annual activity is the Maltina Teacher of the Year (entries 3 June - 7 August 2026, for secondary-school teachers). Check nbplc.com news periodically for any student call.

eligibility.q: Have you seen an open call for an NB-FOETF university scholarship on nbplc.com itself?
eligibility.no: Then there is nothing to apply for yet. Do not trust forms on other sites. Prepare your documents and apply to open awards (SNEPCo, Seplat, MTN, Jim Ovia) meanwhile.

eligibility.q: Are you a student at a Nigerian tertiary institution?
eligibility.no: Secondary-school awards have been made through partners such as Slum2School Africa, not by application to Nigerian Breweries.
Not needed for students. Teachers can enter the Maltina Teacher of the Year, run by the same Trust Fund.

steps.title: Understand what NB-FOETF does today
steps.why: Many websites still list a 'Nigerian Breweries scholarship' with an application link. Knowing the facts protects you from fake calls and wasted time.
do: Open the 2026 Maltina Teacher of the Year article on nbplc.com and read the paragraph about the Trust Fund's history and work.
Open the July 2026 NB-FOETF scholarship article. Note that the student was selected by recognition and the award is managed by a partner.
Write down: 'No open student call found as of Oct 2026'.
Decide to keep watching while you apply to awards that are open.
tips: Official Nigerian Breweries news is on nbplc.com. Treat anything else as unconfirmed until you find it there.
avoid: Paying for a 'Nigerian Breweries scholarship form' on any site.
check: I know there is no confirmed open call right now.

steps.title: Learn to verify any 'Nigerian Breweries scholarship' post
steps.why: Big brands are often used in scam scholarship posts that collect fees or personal data.
do: When you see a call, open nbplc.com yourself and look in the newsroom for the same call.
Check it is free and does not ask for bank PINs, BVN or 'processing fees'.
Check that national newspapers (e.g. The Guardian, BusinessDay, ThisDay) report the same call.
Ask your university's scholarship or Students Affairs office whether they received an official letter.
tips: The application is free. Anyone asking you to pay for a form, 'processing', a test slot or 'guaranteed selection' is a scammer.
Never use an 'agent' or cybercafe operator to apply for you with their email. Use your own email and phone so the funder's messages reach you.
avoid: Trusting a post just because it has the Nigerian Breweries logo.
check: I know three ways to check if a call is real.

links.t: The Guardian: Trust fund awards scholarship to indigent student

steps.title: Set up a simple watch routine
steps.why: If a call appears, corporate windows in Nigeria are often only two to four weeks long.
do: Set a monthly reminder to check the nbplc.com newsroom (education tag).
Follow Nigerian Breweries' official social accounts linked from nbplc.com.
Keep the same reminder for other corporate awards: Seplat (Feb-Mar), MTN (Apr-May), SNEPCo (Jun-Aug), Jim Ovia (Oct-Dec).
tips: Use one calendar for all Nigerian awards so nothing clashes.
avoid: Relying on old blog posts from previous years.
check: My monthly check is in my calendar.

steps.title: Build a ready-to-use document pack
steps.why: Every Nigerian corporate scholarship asks for nearly the same documents. Having them ready lets you apply within days of any call.
do: Get a signed and stamped statement of results showing your CGPA.
Print JAMB and university admission letters, and scan your school ID card.
Scan your WAEC/NECO certificate or result.
Get your LGA identification letter (state of origin) and your NIN slip.
Take a passport photo and save a small JPEG (under 200KB) version.
tips: Name files clearly and keep them in one cloud folder.
avoid: Letting results and letters go out of date - refresh them each session.
check: My document pack is complete and up to date.

links.t: Example of a full document list (SNEPCo 2025)

steps.title: Draft a short personal statement you can adapt
steps.why: Recognition-based awards look for potential and a clear story. A ready statement also helps with Jim Ovia and other need-based awards.
do: Write 300-400 words: who you are, your course and grades, your goals, any challenges (including financial need), and what you have done for others.
Give one concrete example of leadership or service (tutoring, community work, a project).
Ask a lecturer to read it and suggest changes.
Keep it ready to adapt if a call asks for a statement; follow that call's own question and limit.
tips: Use facts and numbers (CGPA, people helped) instead of big words.
Be honest about need without exaggeration.
avoid: Copying a statement from the internet.
check: My draft is clear, honest and under 400 words.
steps.prompt: No official prompt (no open call). Practice: introduce yourself, your goals, a challenge you overcame and your impact on others.

steps.title: Line up a referee
steps.why: Most Nigerian corporate awards ask for a Head of Department letter or similar at short notice.
do: Choose your HOD or a lecturer who knows your work.
Ask if they would write a letter at short notice when a call opens.
Give them a one-page summary: name, matric number, level, CGPA, achievements.
tips: Ask for letters on departmental letterhead, signed, stamped and dated.
avoid: Asking a referee who barely knows you.
check: I have a referee who agreed to help.

steps.title: If an official call appears, apply only through it
steps.why: Only an application through an official Nigerian Breweries route can be considered.
do: Confirm the call is on nbplc.com.
Read eligibility, documents and deadline; check you qualify.
Fill the form with your own email and phone, upload your document pack, and submit early.
Save the confirmation.
avoid: Applying through a third party who asks for money.
check: The call is on nbplc.com and I have proof of submission.

steps.title: Meanwhile, apply to open Nigerian awards
steps.why: Since NB-FOETF has no open student call, your best chances come from other awards with fixed windows.
do: 200 level: NNPC/SNEPCo (Jun-Aug).
200 level and above, listed courses: NNPC/Seplat JV (Feb-Mar).
300 level STEM: MTN Foundation STS (Apr-May).
Any course, financial need: Jim Ovia Foundation (Oct-Dec).
Look also at other brewers' schemes, e.g. the Guinness Nigeria undergraduate scheme, and check their official sites for current calls.
tips: Open each award's guide in Laureate Lab.
avoid: Putting all your hope on one award.
check: I have at least two other awards on my calendar.

links.t: Example of a similar brewer award: Guinness Nigeria Undergraduate Scholarship (2020 call)

steps.title: Teachers: consider Maltina Teacher of the Year
steps.why: This is the Trust Fund's main open competition; it suits graduates who teach in secondary schools.
do: If you teach in a secondary school, read the 2026 MTOY article for rules and prizes.
Watch for the 2027 entry window (2026 ran 3 June - 7 August) at maltinateacheroftheyear.com as linked from nbplc.com.
Prepare evidence of your teaching impact early.
tips: Entries can be submitted online or by email as described in the official article.
check: I know whether MTOY applies to me.

links.t: Nigerian Breweries: 2026 Maltina Teacher of the Year (includes NB-FOETF history)

steps.title: Review twice a year
steps.why: Programmes change. A public student call could return.
do: Every January and July, check nbplc.com news for NB-FOETF updates.
Refresh your document pack and statement.
Update this plan with anything new you find.
tips: Share verified calls with classmates - and warn them about fake ones.
check: My next review date is set.

faq.q: Is there an open Nigerian Breweries university scholarship I can apply for now?
faq.a: Not as of 7 October 2026. No public student application call was found on nbplc.com.

faq.q: Has the Trust Fund given tertiary scholarships before?
faq.a: Yes. Nigerian Breweries says the fund has granted scholarships to deserving students in tertiary institutions, but it has not published a current application process.

faq.q: How was the 2026 scholarship recipient chosen?
faq.a: By recognition: a Slum2School Africa student who gave the keynote at the 2025 Maltina Teacher of the Year finale. The award is administered by Slum2School Africa.

faq.q: I saw a 'Nigerian Breweries scholarship form' online. Is it real?
faq.a: Only if you can find the same call on nbplc.com. Never pay a fee or share bank PINs.

faq.q: What is the Maltina Teacher of the Year?
faq.a: An annual NB-FOETF competition for secondary-school teachers with cash prizes and school projects.
